previous_assumption: assumed a role lookup check of the shape 'existing.organization_id !== organizationId' correctly identifies a role as belonging to a different organization
correction: That condition is also true whenever existing.organization_id is null (the built-in owner role), so it incorrectly 404'd every attempt to reach the SECOND guard (reject editing/deleting the builtin role with 400) before that guard could ever run — caught by a unit test asserting ValidationError and getting NotFoundError instead. Fixed by reusing the already-correct validateRoleForOrganization helper (role.organization_id !== null && role.organization_id !== organizationId) in updateRole/deleteRole too, then checking organization_id === null separately for the builtin guard. Lesson: a nullable discriminator column needs its null case reasoned about explicitly in every comparison, not just the one comparison it was first written for.
